_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 15: Accuracy, Robustness and Cybersecurity
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. Harmonised standards and, where necessary, European standardisation deliverables on accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity specifications for AI systems are being developed under Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, points 6 to 8. No official date for publication of their references in the Official Journal of the European Union has been announced.
basis: EU AI Act Recital 74 (legislative intent on accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity)
ISO/IEC 23894:2023 — Guidance on risk management for AI
ISO/IEC TR 24029-1:2021 — Assessment of the robustness of neural networks — Part 1: Overview
ISO/IEC TR 24029-2:2023 — Assessment of the robustness of neural networks — Part 2: Methodology
MITRE ATLAS — Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems
_metadata.awaiting_standard: Harmonised standards and, where necessary, European standardisation deliverables on accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity specifications for AI systems are being developed under Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, points 6 to 8. No official date for publication of their references in the Official Journal of the European Union has been announced.

requirements.title: Accuracy Metrics Definition and Tracking
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST define, track, and declare accuracy metrics appropriate for the system's intended purpose.
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(1) requires 'an appropriate level of accuracy' and Art. 15(3) requires that 'the levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.' Without defined metrics, compliance cannot be assessed.
required_documentation: Metric values on validation and test sets
Performance breakdown by demographic groups (where applicable)

requirements.title: Testing Infrastructure
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST design and develop the high-risk AI system to achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and take technical and organisational measures for resilience against errors, faults and inconsistencies; unit, integration and model-evaluation tests are possible methods, not individually mandated categories (Article 15(1), (4)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(1) requires an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle, and Art. 15(4) requires high-risk AI systems to be 'as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies', with technical and organisational measures taken in this regard. Testing is a primary way to demonstrate and maintain this.
acceptable_implementations: Unit tests for individual components (pytest, jest, JUnit)
Model evaluation tests (performance on test datasets)
End-to-end tests for critical user flows
requirements.minimum_coverage: Testing SHOULD cover all critical paths and edge cases. Coverage metrics SHOULD be tracked.

requirements.title: Input Validation and Sanitization
requirements.requirement: The provider SHOULD validate inputs at the system's entry points as one of the technical measures for resilience against errors, faults or inconsistencies (Article 15(4)); the Regulation does not prescribe input validation by name.
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(4) requires high-risk AI systems to be 'as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates'. Input validation is a common first line of defence.
acceptable_implementations: Schema validation (pydantic, zod, JSON Schema, Protocol Buffers)
Image/audio/text format validation for ML inputs

requirements.title: Error Handling and Graceful Degradation
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST take technical and organisational measures so that the high-risk AI system is as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies; error handling with graceful degradation is one such measure. Technical redundancy solutions, including backup or fail-safe plans, MAY be used (Article 15(4)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(4): 'High-risk AI systems shall be as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates [...]. Technical and organisational measures shall be taken in this regard. The robustness of high-risk AI systems may be achieved through technical redundancy solutions, which may include backup or fail-safe plans.'
acceptable_implementations: Graceful degradation (fallback to simpler model or rule-based system)
Circuit breaker pattern for external dependencies

requirements.title: Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention
requirements.requirement: The provider SHOULD implement rate limiting on all public-facing endpoints to prevent abuse and denial-of-service attacks.
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(5) requires the technical solutions aiming to ensure the cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems to be 'appropriate to the relevant circumstances and the risks'. Rate limiting is a standard defense against service abuse.
acceptable_implementations: Per-client rate limiting (by IP, API key, or user ID)
Global rate limiting for system protection
Adaptive rate limiting based on threat signals

requirements.title: Authentication and Authorization
requirements.requirement: The provider SHOULD apply authentication and authorisation controls to system endpoints and administrative functions, as appropriate to the relevant circumstances and the risks, as part of the resilience against unauthorised third parties required by Article 15(5).
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(5) requires resilience against 'attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities'. Authentication verifies identity; authorisation enforces access control.
acceptable_implementations: JWT (JSON Web Tokens) with proper validation

requirements.title: Dependency Vulnerability Scanning
requirements.requirement: The provider SHOULD scan third-party dependencies for known vulnerabilities, for example automatically in the development pipeline, as part of the resilience against the exploitation of system vulnerabilities required by Article 15(5).
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(5) requires protection against exploitation of 'system vulnerabilities.' Third-party dependencies are a common attack vector.
acceptable_implementations: Dependabot or Renovate for automated updates
Trivy or Grype for container scanning
CodeQL or SonarQube for static analysis

requirements.title: Adversarial Testing
requirements.requirement: The provider SHOULD perform adversarial testing proportionate to relevant AI-specific vulnerabilities, potentially including data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples/model evasion and confidentiality attacks; Article 15(5) requires appropriate cybersecurity solutions, not a specifically named testing regimen.
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(5) requires the technical solutions to address AI specific vulnerabilities to include, where appropriate, measures against attacks trying to manipulate the training data set (data poisoning) or pre-trained components used in training (model poisoning), inputs designed to cause the AI model to make a mistake (adversarial examples or model evasion), confidentiality attacks or model flaws. Model inversion and membership inference are not named in the Regulation; they are common examples of confidentiality attacks.
acceptable_implementations: Red team exercises for AI systems
attack_types_to_test: Data poisoning: Can training data be manipulated?
Model poisoning: Can pre-trained components used in training be manipulated?
Adversarial examples or model evasion: Can adversarial inputs cause misclassification?
Confidentiality attacks, e.g. model inversion: Can model outputs reveal training data?
Confidentiality attacks, e.g. membership inference: Can membership in the training set be detected?

requirements.title: Redundancy and Failover
requirements.requirement: The provider MAY employ technical redundancy, including backup or fail-safe plans, as an approach to robustness appropriate to the system's risks; Article 15(4) does not require redundancy.
requirements.rationale: Art. 15(4): 'The robustness of high-risk AI systems may be achieved through technical redundancy solutions, which may include backup or fail-safe plans.' For production systems, this often means infrastructure redundancy.

scoring.compliant: R01 + R02 + R06 met, and at least 4 of R03-R05, R07-R09 met
scoring.partial: R01 or R02 met + at least 4 others met
scoring.non_compliant: Neither R01 nor R02 met, or fewer than 4 requirements met
